sections.title: Standard notation
sections.extract: []{#xxsec1.1 label="xxsec1.1"} Let $k$ be a commutative base field, arbitrary for the moment. When we are working with quantum groups it will sometimes be necessary to assume that $k$ contains ${\mathbb C}(q)$. Unless stated otherwise all vector spaces are over $k$, and an unadorned $\otimes$ will mean $\otimes_k$. An algebra or a ring always means a $k$-algebra with associative multiplication $m_A$ and with unit 1.
